title: Orion Command and Priority Orchestration - All Hands
customer_attendees: various folks from Eng, Product, Sales, People
summary: Quarterly all-hands focused on priorities for the next 60 days: product shipping cadence, reliability investments, hiring cadence changes, and an operational plank called Orion to unify rollouts. Leadership announced a new initiative to reduce P95 latency for short-chat paths, clarified Dedicated vs Private prioritization, and committed to a 6-week decision freeze on new major integrations while we stabilize the runtime. Townhall included a short incident postmortem, budget constraints, and Q&A on headcount and compensation cadence.

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-04-02
Time: 10:00 AM PT
Duration: ~72 minutes
Attendees: Elena Morales, Samir Patel, Lina Cho, Marcus Reed, Priya Nair, Jonah Blake + all-hands

Summary (auto): Leadership update on 'Orion' orchestration initiative, reliability focus, short-term hiring/compensation guidance, and next steps.

Transcript:
[00:00] Samir: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we'll kick off in a minute. Uh, can folks mute unless you're speaking, please.
[00:18] Elena: Morning team, welcome to the April all-hands, appreciate everyone making time. Quick outline: Samir will walk platform updates, Lina will cover engineering priorities and Orion, Marcus will cover people changes, Priya on GTM and pilots, then Q&A.
[00:45] Samir: Cool, first thing, small ops update. We've pushed a set of kernel pulls that's improved throughput on the long sequence paths; however, short-chat P95 is still above target, and that's... that's our north star for product calls. We're calling the program Orion — it's basically a routing/orchestration and rollout framework so we can pin low-latency variants for short sequences.
[01:20] Audience: (murmurs)
[01:30] Lina: Right, Orion is an internal codename. The idea is to unify model routing, KV cache policies, and autoscaling triggers for the two dominant latency profiles: short-chat (<= 64 tokens) and long-context. We've instrumented in staging, but there are some edge cases with continuous batching that actually regresses p95 for under 100ms scenarios.
[02:05] Samir: To be clear, we want predictable p95 for interactive features; we are not trying to squeeze last microsecond out of everything, it's about consistent user experience.
[02:30] Elena: On the business side, we have three pilots lined up — Bluegrid (partner), a fintech customer, and an education use-case. Bluegrid asked for a VPC option and audit logs with KMS. We've told them Dedicated isn't fully hardened for their audit timeline, but Private can work with some help from Security.
[03:05] Marcus: Quick people update — we are instituting a controlled hiring pause for IC hiring in some squads while we focus on critical reliability hires and role leveling. We heard the feedback on comp cadence, so we'll share an updated timeline. This is not a layoff — it's a prioritization.
[03:39] Audience / Q: Is this a freeze across the company?
[03:45] Marcus: Not a full freeze. Sales-facing quota roles and critical engineering reliability roles kept open. We will publish the matrix by next Friday.
[04:10] Priya: On pilots and revenue, we are delaying a few enterprise integration commitments by 6 weeks — that's the freeze Elena mentioned — to avoid overlapping large rollouts. We'll keep marketing and sales aligned on messaging.
[04:35] Lina: Technical deep dive — some notes. The root cause for the recent P95 regression: KV cache eviction policy + batching heuristics interacting badly under bursty short requests. In practice, when small requests come in, we coalesce them into batches that increase serialization latency for the first token. Fixes: (1) shard-level micro-batching for short paths, (2) lower-latency kernel selection for quantized ops, (3) smarter warm KV cache priming.
[05:12] Samir: Jonah's team is running a benchmark to validate these changes. Jonah?
[05:18] Jonah: We're going to run a 72-hour sweep with synthetic traffic approximating our top 10 customers' short chat percentiles. We'll share the spreadsheet and the runbook. Expect noise in the first 24 hours as the cache warms.
[05:40] Audience: (typing)
[06:02] Elena: On reliability SLOs: we're tightening alerts for P95 and introducing a daily health signal for core serving, visible in Console. Also rolling out per-route cost telemetry so product managers can see unit economics.
[06:25] Samir: A note on model variants: for low-latency traffic we'll provision smaller quantized variants with fallback to full models for higher-quality completions. That is policy controlled; product can pin per-route.
[06:52] Q: Any impact to pricing?
[06:56] Priya: No immediate change to public pricing; we will model dedicated/private cost uplift for pilot customers and be transparent.
[07:18] Marcus: People question — we heard concerns about transparency during this period. We'll host a AMA next Wednesday, timezone-friendly sessions. Compensation review cadence: still on track for Q3 but the committee requested an extra audit step, so we'll detail that next week.
[07:45] Lina: On testing, we will extend synthetic perf regression suite to include short path microbenchmarks — this will catch regressions earlier in CI.
[08:05] Elena: I'll cover a brief incident recap from last month: a misrouted fallback caused a spike in token costs and increased latency for a subset of requests — the rollback was immediate, but the follow-up is a fix in our routing policy to avoid cross-variant fallback during peak. Action: finalize routing change and do a canary.
[08:42] Samir: The canary must include KV cache warmers, else first token P95 will still spike, so include priming.
[09:00] Audience Member (transcript: Speaker 3): "Is Orion just for short-chat?"
[09:05] Lina: No, Orion is a framework. Short-chat is the first priority because it's where product adoption is most sensitive. Long context tools get different autoscaling and batching profiles.
[09:25] Priya: On go-to-market — pilots: Bluegrid wants a compliance pack; we will provide SOC artifacts and a partner-focused integration plan. We need security to sign off; Elena will coordinate.
[09:45] Elena: Yep, Security will work with Bluegrid's auditors. Jonah, can you support a private benchmark for them next week?
[09:53] Jonah: Yes, will do.
[10:00] [10:00] Q&A:
[10:05] Q: "What does the 6-week freeze mean for roadmap features?"
[10:09] Elena: It means we'll de-prioritize new external integrations and marketing-led big launches; smaller UX polish and reliability work continues.
[10:20] Q: "How do we measure success for Orion?"
[10:23] Lina: Metrics: P95 short-chat latency (target <= 200ms regional median), tail-error rate, and cost-per-1000 tokens for short path. Follow-on: customer satisfaction for chat UIs.
[10:40] Q: "Are we re-evaluating Dedicated vs Private investments?"
[10:44] Samir: We're keeping both but shifting near-term engineering attention to Private for compliance-heavy pilots and to Dedicated for predictable throughput customers. We'll publish the investment rubric.
[11:00] Marcus: People ops Q: "If hiring is paused, what's the plan for backfills?"
[11:05] Marcus: Critical backfills go through the hiring council; most roles will convert to internal transfers where possible. We'll avoid external hires unless approved.
[11:30] Elena: A note about experimentation: we're standardizing rollouts with canary percentages tied to latency SLOs; automatic rollback if p95 jumps > 25% in the canary window. That helps us move faster with less risk.
[12:00] Priya: Revenue update — Q2 bookings on track, but some large deals will shift by a quarter if pilots need more time. We reforecast next week once pilot dates are locked.
[12:35] Audience: (applause)
[12:50] Closing remarks: Elena: I'm proud of the team's responsiveness. This is a moment to be deliberate — Orion will give us predictable user experiences. We'll keep comms frequent.
[13:05] Action recap: Lina to write RFC; Jonah to run benchmarks; Priya to publish pilot intake; Marcus to publish hiring matrix; leadership to share decision rubric.
[13:25] Samir: Thanks everyone, meeting adjourned.

Notes about transcription: occasional name mis-recognition (Bluegrid sometimes transcribed as "BlueGrid" or "Blue grad"), technical acronyms sometimes split (K V cache, KMS as K-M-S), and speaker overlap in the Q&A.
